styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: The Guggenheim, the Fine Arts Museum and riverside walks.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Pintxos bars, market halls and txakoli wine.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: The old town, the river and Basque traditions.

stays.why: Old-town lanes, pintxos bars and the cathedral on your doorstep; metro and tram nearby.
Central and handy: main train station, shops and a short walk to the Guggenheim.
Quiet, local feel with good restaurants; between the old town and the museum district.
University area across the river; cheaper rooms and a short metro or tram ride to the centre.

food: Eat pintxos standing at the bar: small plates on bread, €2–4 each. Point at what you want and keep your toothpicks for the bill.
The Mercado de la Ribera by the river is a good stop for fresh produce and casual bites; check opening days on the day.
Try bacalao (salt cod) dishes and txakoli, the local slightly sparkling white wine.
Lunch is the main meal; many restaurants offer a menú del día around €12–18 on weekdays.
Dinner starts late, often after 20:30. Bars are busiest Thursday to Saturday.
more_time: Take the Artxanda funicular for a hilltop view over the city; a short ride and cheap ticket.
Day trip to the coast: train to Mundaka or Bermeo for fishing villages and the coast.
Swap a museum afternoon for the Bizkaia Bridge (Puente Colgante) in Getxo, a UNESCO site, by metro.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Guggenheim, the old town and a proper pintxos crawl; add a night for a coast or hill day.

month_notes: January: cool and wet, highs near 12°C and about 15 rain days. Pack a rain jacket.
February: still cool and showery, highs around 14°C. Quiet museums.
March: mild at 16°C but the wettest month, about 17 rain days. Bring an umbrella.
April: pleasant at 17°C with fewer wet days. Good for walking.
May: warming to 20°C and mostly dry-ish. A lovely month.
June: mild and bright, highs near 23°C. Long evenings outdoors.
July: warmest and driest, highs about 25°C with around 10 rain days. Busy.
August: hot at 26°C and dry. Book ahead; beaches get crowded.
September: still warm at 24°C with a little more rain. Good value.
October: cooler at 21°C and wetter, about 13 rain days. Bring layers.
November: cool and rainy, highs near 16°C and 16 rain days. Indoor plans.
December: cool at 14°C with about 14 rain days. Festive but damp.

climate_guide.summary: Oceanic climate: mild all year, rain in every month, and rarely very hot or cold.

items.title: Rain any month
items.text: Expect 10–17 rain days every month. March and November are wettest. Always carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Mild temperatures
items.text: Highs run from about 12°C in January to 26°C in August. Rarely freezing, rarely hot.

items.title: Best months: June to September
items.text: Warmest and driest, highs 23–26°C with fewer rain days. Best for the river and the coast.

items.title: Layers, not heavy coats
items.text: Mornings and evenings are cool even in summer. A light jacket and a rain layer cover most trips.

items.title: Grey skies are normal
items.text: Cloudy days are common. Plan museums and pintxos bars as backup on wet days.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable walking shoes, a waterproof jacket and an umbrella. Sunglasses for summer.

transit.best: Walk the centre and use the metro or tram for longer hops; get a Barik card.

modes.text: Clean and fast. Single tickets cost about €1.70–1.95 by zone.
The green Euskotren tram runs along the river past the Guggenheim; single ticket €1.50.
Bilbobus city buses are red with a flat fare; Bizkaibus green buses serve the province.
Taxis are easy to find; ride apps like Uber and Bolt operate in Bilbao.
Driving is hard: hilly one-ways, works, and a low emissions zone. Walk or cycle instead.
Best for the old town and riverside. The centre is compact and walkable.
